title: What was the light of the first three days, before the lights of the fourth?
summary: Genesis 1 has light, Day and Night, and three evenings and mornings before the lights in the firmament are made on the fourth day “to divide the day from the night”. The passage does not say what the earlier light was or where it came from.
text: KJV Genesis 1:3: “And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.” Hebrew (WLC) 1:3: יְהִ֣י אֹ֑ור וַֽיְהִי־אֹֽור [let there be light, and there was light]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 1:3: γενηθήτω φῶς· καὶ ἐγένετο φῶς [let there be light, and there was light]. KJV 1:4: “and God divided the light from the darkness”. KJV 1:5: “And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And the evening and the morning were the first day.” KJV 1:14: “And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night”. Hebrew (WLC) 1:14: יְהִ֤י מְאֹרֹת֙ בִּרְקִ֣יעַ הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם [let there be lights in the firmament of the heavens]. Brenton Greek 1:14: γενηθήτωσαν φωστῆρες ἐν τῷ στερεώματι τοῦ οὐρανοῦ [let there be light-givers in the firmament of the heaven]. KJV 1:16: “And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.” KJV 1:18: “and to divide the light from the darkness”. KJV Job 38:19: “Where is the way where light dwelleth?” KJV Isaiah 45:7: “I form the light, and create darkness”. KJV 2 Corinthians 4:6: “God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/1/1/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/GEN01.htm.
reasoning: On the first day there is light, it is divided from the darkness, the two are named Day and Night, and an evening and a morning are counted. The second and third days are counted the same way. Only on the fourth day are the lights made, and their stated work is the same: to divide the day from the night, to give light on the earth, and to divide the light from the darkness. The passage does not say what the light of verses 3–5 was, what gave it, or what marked evening and morning before the fourth day. The Hebrew uses one noun for the light of the first day and a different, related noun for the lights of the fourth; Brenton’s Greek does the same.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. The record does not say that light needs the Sun, and it does not say the passage is mistaken. Several explanations are offered by readers: light given directly by God; lights that already existed and were only appointed or made visible on the fourth day; an order that is not meant as a sequence in time. Each is an interpretation; the passage states none of them. The published record genesis-1-celestial-sequence deals with vegetation before the Sun on a literal timeline; this record does not repeat it. Check made for an answer elsewhere: the packaged KJV was searched for “light” and “lights” (243 verses), and those that also speak of darkness together with making, forming, commanding or dividing were read, with Job 38:19. The three quoted are the closest; none names a source for the light of Genesis 1:3. That is a word search, not a reading of the whole Bible, and it does not prove that no passage addresses the question. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined. The Greek is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. It is not a critical apparatus and does not show that all Greek witnesses agree or which reading is original. English in square brackets is the researcher’s plain rendering, not a KJV quotation and not a lexicon entry.

title: Who were the people Cain feared would slay him?
summary: After killing Abel, Cain says that every one who finds him will slay him, and the Lord marks him so that no one finding him will kill him. The passage does not say who these people were.
text: KJV Genesis 4:1: “And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain”. KJV 4:2: “And she again bare his brother Abel.” KJV 4:14: “and I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond in the earth; and it shall come to pass, that every one that findeth me shall slay me”. Hebrew (WLC) 4:14: וְהָיָ֥ה כָל־מֹצְאִ֖י יַֽהַרְגֵֽנִי [and it shall be, everyone finding me will kill me]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 4:14: καὶ ἔσται πᾶς ὁ εὑρίσκων με, ἀποκτενεῖ με [and it shall be, everyone who finds me will kill me]. KJV 4:15: “And the Lord said unto him, Therefore whosoever slayeth Cain, vengeance shall be taken on him sevenfold. And the Lord set a mark upon Cain, lest any finding him should kill him.” KJV 4:25: “And Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth”. KJV 5:4: “and he begat sons and daughters”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/1/4/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/GEN04.htm.
reasoning: Up to this point the book has named four people: Adam, Eve, Cain and Abel, and Abel is dead. Cain expects that whoever finds him will kill him, and the Lord’s answer treats the danger as real enough to guard against. The passage does not say who might find him, where they lived, or how they were related to him.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. That only four people have been named does not show that only four existed; the book does not say so either way. Genesis 5:4 says Adam had other sons and daughters, without saying when they were born; that they or their children are meant is one reading. That other people are meant is another. Neither is stated, and the record does not assert any kinship. Check made for an answer elsewhere: every verse of the packaged KJV outside Genesis that contains the name Cain was read (Hebrews 11:4, 1 John 3:12, Jude 1:11; Joshua 15:57 is a town). None speaks of the people Cain feared. That is a word search, not a reading of the whole Bible. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined. The Greek is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. title: Who was Cain’s wife, and where did she come from?
summary: Genesis says Cain knew his wife and she bore Enoch. It does not name her or say who her parents were, and no woman other than Eve has been mentioned before this verse.
text: KJV Genesis 4:1: “And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain”. KJV 4:16: “And Cain went out from the presence of the Lord, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.” KJV 4:17: “And Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city”. Hebrew (WLC) 4:17: וַיֵּ֤דַע קַ֙יִן֙ אֶת־אִשְׁתֹּ֔ו [and Cain knew his wife]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 4:17: Καὶ ἔγνω Κάϊν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ [and Cain knew his wife]. KJV 5:4: “And the days of Adam after he had begotten Seth were eight hundred years: and he begat sons and daughters”. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/1/4/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/GEN04.htm.
reasoning: The wife appears in the story without a name, a parent or a place of origin. Before this verse the only woman mentioned is Eve, Cain’s mother. Whether Cain married before or after he went to Nod is not said either: verse 16 puts him in Nod and verse 17 speaks of his wife without saying where he found her.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. Many people in the Bible are unnamed; the question here is her origin, since the book has not yet mentioned any family she could come from. Genesis 5:4 says Adam had daughters, without saying when; that Cain married a sister or a niece is a reading drawn from that verse, not a statement of the text. That she came from other people is another reading, also unstated. The record asserts neither. The city Cain builds in the same verse raises a like question about its inhabitants; it is not pursued here. Check made for an answer elsewhere: every verse of the packaged KJV outside Genesis that contains the name Cain was read (Hebrews 11:4, 1 John 3:12, Jude 1:11; Joshua 15:57 is a town). None mentions his wife. That is a word search, not a reading of the whole Bible. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined. The Greek is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. It is not a critical apparatus and does not show that all Greek witnesses agree or which reading is original.
